test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In 1798, who became the Governor General and built a massive palace, Government House, for himself in Calcutta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Wellesley.**__

__
 
• **Lord Wellesley** became the Governor General and built a massive palace, Government House, for himself in Calcutta.

 
 
• He was a Governor-General of India between **1798 and 1805.**
 
• Lord Wellesley was appointed Governor General of Bengal in** 1798 at the age of 37**.
 
• He had two main objectives in India
 
 
• To make the East India Company the supreme and sovereign power in India.
 
• To increase the area under the control of the company. 
 
 
 
• Its second major goal was to eliminate French influence in India and to prevent potential regional expansion of France into India.
 
• **Madras Presidency **was formed during the tenure of Lord Wellesley.
 
• Fort William College was set up by Lord Wellesley in 1800 for the training of civil servants of the Company in languages and customs of Indians 
 
• **Censorship of Press Act, 1799** was enacted by Lord Wellesley, anticipating the French invasion of India.

• **Lord William Bentinck **served as **Governor-General of Bengal and India from 1828 to 1835**.

 
 
• Along with Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Bentinck tried to suppress many superstitious practices like Sati, the practice of widow burning.
 
• It was abolished by the Bengal Sati Regulation, passed in 1829.
 
• He also tried to control practices like polygamy, child marriages and caste rigidity.
 
 
 
• **Robert Clive** became the Governor of Bengal twice once from 1757-1760 and other from 1765-1767.
 
 
• The Dual System of Government was established by him in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793)** introduced the system of Daroga as part of Police reforms.
 
 
• Police of each district was placed under District Judge.
 
• Each district was divided into Thanas/Police circles which will be headed by Daroga, an Indian officer assisted by constables.
